transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm here because... well, it's my face. The left side of it, mostly. I just... I can't stop thinking about how off it looks. Like my nose and my jaw, they just look crooked. I see it in every ID photo, and whenever I have to turn my camera on for online classes. People tell me they don't see it, but... I don't know. When I'm in the CNC lab, I just feel like everyone is staring at it. Like they see my face before they even look at my work.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly to try to fix or check the way your face looks, like adjusting your posture, using makeup, or touching your face?

Yeah, I... I guess I do check it a lot. 

Before I leave for school, I usually... well, I get stuck in the bathroom. Just looking in the mirror. Or I'll use my phone camera to check the angles. I try to fix my hair to cover it, or... or I'll keep changing shirts to see if maybe a different collar makes my jaw look less crooked. 

I ask my mom sometimes if it looks weird, but... I don't know. Sometimes I'm just doing all that for so long that I end up missing my lab entirely. Or if I do make it, I'm just... I'm too wiped out to even focus on my work.
Does this concern about your face cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life, like going to school or spending time with friends?

Yeah, it does. Um... it messes things up. 

I've missed a lot of my CNC labs. And my shifts at the shop. Sometimes I just... I can't get out the door. My faculty mentor actually talked to me about it. He said my work placement might be in jeopardy if I keep missing hours. 

And... I don't really do much else anymore. I used to play soccer, and I volunteered, but I stopped. I just... I don't want people looking at me. So I stay home.
Have you ever felt certain that your face looks a certain way, even when others have told you it doesn’t or when photos don’t show what you see?
Um... I guess so. I mean, my mom says it looks fine. But I know what I see. I don't really know what else to say about it.
Can you tell me more about how you feel when you look in the mirror? Like, what exactly goes through your mind when you're checking your face?

Um... I just... I mostly just focus on how off the left side of my face looks. Like, my nose and my jaw. They just look really crooked to me. 

I see it every time I look, or in... in any ID photo, or on the camera for my online classes. I just can't stop thinking about it. And... I know people say they don't see it, but I just feel like everyone in the CNC lab is staring at it. Like they notice my face being messed up before they even notice my work. 

That's... that's mainly what I'm thinking about.

When you look at your face and see the crookedness on the left side, is this something you believe others can clearly see and are likely noticing, or do you feel like it's something only you can really tell?
Um... I mean... I think they can see it. I feel like they do. I don't know... it's just what I think.

When you look at your face and see the crookedness, do you believe that the defect is obvious to others, or do you think it's something that only you can really notice but worry others might judge you for?
Um... I think they notice it. I mean, it's pretty obvious to me. So... yeah, I'm pretty sure they see it and judge me for it. I don't know what else to say.

When you look at your face and feel that the left side looks crooked, do you believe that the issue you see is something that others would clearly notice and comment on, or is it something that you feel only you can see but still worry about?
I just... I don't really know for sure. I mean, I feel like they can see it. It's just what I think. I don't really talk to them about it, so... I don't know if they'd actually say anything.
Is it mainly the way your face looks that bothers you, or is it more about how others might judge you in general when they look at you?

Um... I guess it's both. I just... I can't stop thinking about how the left side looks. It's just off. Like my nose and jaw are crooked. I see it in every ID photo... or on camera for my online classes. And... I don't know, even when people tell me they don't see it, I feel like everyone in the CNC lab is noticing it. Like they see my face before they even look at my work. So... yeah. That's mostly why I came in.
When you're worried about how your face looks, is your main concern that others are noticing and judging your appearance, or is it more about how you see yourself in general, even when you're alone?

Um... I'm not really sure. I guess... both? 

It bothers me when I'm by myself, too. I just... I don't like how it looks.

When you're most upset about how your face looks, is your main worry that people are noticing and criticizing your appearance, or is it more about how you feel about your face, even when you're alone and not around others?
Um... I don't really know what else to say about it. I mean... like I just said, I guess it's both. I just always hate how it looks, no matter where I am. I don't really know how to separate it.
Are you also very concerned about other parts of your body or appearance, or is your main worry specifically about how your face looks when other people see you?

Um... no. Not really other parts. Just... like I said before, it's my face. The left side. I just can't stop focusing on my nose and jaw being crooked... on camera, or when I'm at the lab. That's... that's the whole reason I came in. It's just my face.

When you're looking at your face and feeling upset about how it looks, is your main concern that others are seeing you negatively because of it, or is it more about how you perceive the appearance of your face itself?
I... didn't you just ask me that? I don't really have a different answer for you. I just... I see it, and I know they see it. I don't know what else to tell you.

When you feel upset about how your face looks, do you feel like you have to do certain things, like checking mirrors, adjusting your clothes, or asking others for reassurance, even if you know it might not help?

Um... yeah, I guess. I mean, before I leave for school... I just get stuck. Like, in the bathroom mirror, or I use my phone camera. I just keep checking it. And... I try to fix my hair, or I'll change my shirt to try and hide the angle of my jaw. Sometimes I ask my mom if it looks weird. It just... takes a long time. Sometimes I do it for so long I just miss my lab entirely. Or if I do go, I'm just too wiped out to even focus on the CNC machines. So... yeah, I do that stuff.
